`goatbuilder`, the build, release, deploy and standup tool for a goatnet.

**New in 0.8.0.** *Act on these before you run this release:* (1) `goatbuilder deploy` and `deploy-component.sh` now verify the goatnet's signed intent from the checkout before any host: the intent is there, its signature verifies against its CA's committed public key, it is what the tree renders, and each member group's `pins.yml` is what the pins table renders. One that does not hold is refused with GB-383, exit 1. A goatnet whose intent was never signed, or whose pins moved without signing again, can no longer be deployed with either tool: sign its intent and commit it before you deploy; `ops/pins/generate-pins.py --check --goatnet <name>` shows what would be refused. `deploy-component.sh` now needs the Python module `jsonschema` beside PyYAML (#1226). (2) Deploy refuses a pin with no `@sha256:` digest before any host, with GB-382: the digest must be in the pin's value, not a trailing comment, and be 64 lowercase hex characters; pin every component you deploy by digest. `deploy --dry-run`, with either tool, now runs the fresh-source check and the secrets gate as a real run does, fetches the trunk (`--offline` judges against the cached one), prints the whole plan and exits 1 when a real run would refuse, where it ended `ok`, exit 0; a script that runs a dry run should read its exit (#1225). (3) `goatbuilder deploy` now applies the release-ladder gate, GB-373, as `deploy-component.sh` does: it refuses when the rung below pins another digest or does not pin the component, and a real run reads the rung below's ledgers and refuses unless it converged. A recorded exception takes `--skip-rung --reason "<why>" --ack "<operator>"`, written to the deploy ledger (#1187). (4) a joining site whose group_vars set no `zenoh_stack` is refused by `join-node` before any phase runs, with GB-361; add `zenoh_stack: <site_id>-zenoh` to `group_vars/<site>_hosts/` (#1130). (5) A site that keeps its own `ops/ansible/<site>-seed-from-peer.yml` needs a first line `# derived-from: site-seed-from-peer.yml sha256:<digest>`, or `standup` (phase 6) and `join-node` (phase 13) refuse it with GB-362; the refusal prints the digest to set once the copy is brought up to date with the generic play (#1129, #1179). (6) `join-node` and every `standup` phase now refuse, before the phase runs, a command that would read an unset environment variable, with GB-369 naming the phase and each variable; set the variables it names, for example `OWNER_EMAIL` on a founder, before the run (#1164, #1176). (7) `join-node` refuses a plan in which a health publisher the site runs has no leaf certificate in `ops/enrollment/manifests/<site>-certs.yaml`, with GB-364; add the leaf, or declare the publisher absent (#1165). (8) The stack watcher on a management host (`mgmt-host-compose-watch`) is now paused for the whole of a deploy and starts only once the stack is up. A deploy that fails partway keeps the pause, says so and prints the command that clears it; while it is paused the watcher restarts nothing. A new alert, `ComposeWatchPaused`, fires when a pause lasts over 30 minutes, and a reboot clears it. After a failed deploy, clear the pause or re-run the deploy (#1172). When `site-bootstrap.yml` refuses a joiner's Postgres cluster for its encoding, pause the watcher first with the reason `postgres-reinit`, as the refusal says; the re-run clears that pause (#1128). (9) To remove the unused `pgbackrest-runner` sidecar from a host, deploy the pgbackrest role: it removes the container, `docker-compose.pgbackrest.yml` and the `PGBACKREST_IMAGE` line in `.env`, and leaves the repository alone. It first stops and names any file in the repository, log or spool directory that the database user does not own; fix that ownership yourself, because backups and restore fail on such files. `endstate` now grades pgBackRest from its acceptance rows, not from that container (#1103). (10) Scripts that read exit codes: see *Changed exit codes* below. *For someone deploying:* A component of `ops/pins/fleet-pins.yaml` may ship as a signed release file (`artifact_type: release`, with a `release:` mapping of its checksums file, a file per architecture and the workflow that signs it, with no ref), pinned as `<owner>/<repository>@<tag>@sha256:<digest>`: `deploy`, `verify`, `rollback`, `promote` and `fastlane` take it, on both avenues, and fetch and verify it on the operator's machine before any host (GB-365, GB-381, GB-379); `status`, `diff` and `survey` list it, and a deploy that follows a rollback to the same ref now writes its own ledger row (#1210, #1228, #1229, #1232). A component may instead declare `source:`, a play in another repository at a full commit, fetched with your own git access and held to that commit (GB-385, #1236); for both kinds `deploy-component.sh` needs goatbuilder on PATH, or `GOATBUILDER_BIN`. `join-node` and `standup` read each machine type from a file in `ops/goatbuilder/targets/` and the hardware a type accepts from `ops/goatbuilder/families/`; every plan is unchanged, and a private overlay can add types and families in `ops/goatbuilder/overlay/` (GB-374 to GB-378, #1205). A type may list `services:`, which `join-node` phase 13 deploys to the machine (GB-384), and `deploy --group <group> --node <machine>` deploys to one machine of a group (#1235). `goatbuilder doctor --target <type> --site <site>` checks a site's machines of one type against its file and reaches no host (#1212). Two new types: `federation-boundary`, the machine `goatbuilder federate` makes peerings on (#1238), and `network-tap`, whose machines declare `tap:` with `mode: listen` (fail-open) or `mode: inline` (fail-closed), refused with GB-380 when it is missing or wrong; `doctor --target network-tap --live` checks a tap on the machine and `status` prints its mode. Its phase 13 installs goatrope, the tap's installer, as a release component where the pins pin it, after phase 3 has run `deploy --dry-run` for it; goatrope has no release yet, so a machine joined as `network-tap` today is not a working tap (#1227, #1230, #1231). `fastlane` reads and pins an image under the owner its fleet ref names, not this checkout's (#1234). Five acceptance rows check the break-glass node's out-of-band route and the network-gear jump box (#1237). `ops/ansible/netbird-acl-cutover.yml -e cut_off=true`, and the access-rule bootstrap with the same flag, is for a site cut off from the others: it only updates the policies the site already has, by id, and refuses with GB-295 a run that would create or delete one; after the heal, run both at the hub without `cut_off`. Without the flag both run as before (#708). Every error the rest of goatbuilder raises now carries its catalog code, so a log of a run that met one names the code and `goatbuilder explain <code>` answers it. They use existing codes where one fits, and three are new: GB-326, a file of the checkout that is not YAML; GB-359, `federate allocate` naming a peering the config does not declare; and GB-365, a pins file that breaks the pins schema or its rules (#920, #1093, #1139). Five checks inside `goatbuilder federate` now carry a code too (GB-315, GB-321, GB-277). A failed step's row prints its own catalog code: GB-183 for a `federate` phase, and five new codes, GB-331 to GB-335, for a `standup` phase, a `join-node` phase, standup's image pull, an observability leg and a `teardown` stop (#920). When the preflight finds a variable still holding a secret reference (`op://`, `bao://`, `bw://`), it refuses with GB-368, and `explain` now says to run the command through `ops/scripts/with-secrets` or unset the variable, where it used to suggest a `git pull` (#1161). A run record's probe log now names only the variables the verb reads, not every variable set on the machine; values were never printed (#1162). `goatbuilder explain teardown` and `explain federate-backout` answer for each of their steps; nothing a run does changes (#864). `status` and `verify` in `-o json` carry `machines`, one entry per graded machine with its state (`converged`, `pending` or `unknown`) and a reason from a closed set; the text pages and exit codes are unchanged (#1095). `goatbuilder update` checks a release against a list of release signers it carries, beside the checkout's `repo.release_source`, and run outside a checkout it no longer stops with GB-078; when no signer matches, GB-261 names each signer and why it refused (#1036). `goatbuilder federate rotate <partner> ipsec-leaf` and `ipsec-ca` check more on the edge: the rotation refuses a strongSwan series it was not tested with (5.9 and 6.0 are), with GB-341, refuses a staged leaf on the live leaf's key (GB-290) and an edge where another peering lacks its files (GB-343), and confirms that charon lists exactly one certificate of our id, the new leaf's, before it keeps the new pair; otherwise the old pair is put back (GB-342). Measured on strongSwan 5.9.8 and 6.0.4 (#962). A peering's `forwarder:` takes the forwarder machine's `ansible_user`, `public_interface` and `ssh_sources`, and `federate allocate` writes them into the forwarder's group file, so the forwarder needs no hand-written host file; peerings on one forwarder that declare different values are refused with GB-339 (#934). A fault a federation verb's library raises now prints the new code GB-338 under the same message, and still exits 1 (#937). A peering in `goatbuilder.yaml` may declare `package: v1` (the default, as every peering has run) or `package: v2` (ADR 1242, the announcement of a next CA); this release runs v1 only, and `goatbuilder validate` refuses `package: v2` with GB-025 (#898). Phase 6 composes the agreement only with the peering's declared partner (`FED_COUNTERPARTY_ID`): a counterparty package of another party is refused with GB-191 and no agreement is written, even when a shared keyring binds that party's key; `goat federate compose` takes the parties as `--party <sovereign_id>` (#871). `ops/goatbuilder/c3-measure.sh --env <goatnet> --out <directory>` runs gate row C3's check on a standing goatnet as one command and changes nothing: it exits 0 when `status`, `diff` and `verify` agree on every machine, 3 on a disagreement and 2 when the run is not a measurement (#866). `goatbuilder join-node` runs from phase 1 to 15 with no operator step: phase 1 is now a check that the node answers over SSH (or a phone over USB), and a node that does not answer stops the run with GB-314, which also says which case it hit when ssh fails and prints nothing; resume with `--from 1` (#869, #1048). `join-node` reads `goatnet_founder` with Ansible's booleans, as site bootstrap does, a joiner's run no longer needs `OWNER_EMAIL`, and phase 15 runs the acceptance rows against the site's end state, so a row for a service the site declares absent reads N/A (#869). `goatbuilder join-node` gives a joining site its secrets in phase 3: the values every site of a goatnet shares are taken from the founder's, the site's own are minted, and nothing is overwritten; a differing or missing value is refused with GB-352, GB-353 or GB-354 (#1037). A joining site no longer creates a second identity for each site administrator: the bootstrap administrator is created only at a founder site, and a joiner's identities arrive from the founder (#1124). Phase 13 compares every seed table on the founder and the joiner before it wires replication and again after, and a table that differs stops the run with GB-367, naming the table and both row counts; re-seed and resume with `--from 13` (#1178). `join-node <env> --site <site> --node <node> --class <class> --reseed` copies a replicating node again from its founder when the node was away long enough to lose its replication slot: six journaled steps, a rerun starts at the step that stopped, and `--dry-run` prints them (#1117). From phase 12 on, `join-node` reaches the node at its mesh address, so a node whose LAN address stops answering after enrolment no longer stops the run at phase 14 (#1126). A joining site with no observability host of its own gets Prometheus, Alertmanager and the exporters on its node at the end of phase 13, with Grafana left off; the step needs `obs_colocated_site_zones` in the site's group_vars and `<SITE>_POSTGRES_EXPORTER_PASS` in the environment, and without them it is skipped and says what is missing (#1102). A standup phase now passes secrets to its play through the environment, not the command line; the same variables must be set, and an empty one is refused before the phase runs (#1038). A standup play limited to the founder's management host is refused with GB-355 when the limit matches no host, where it used to pass having done nothing (#974). `teardown` asks each host whether a component is there before it stops it, reports "nothing to stop" for one that never ran, also stops the LAN name server, the LAN Traefik and the SPIRE agent, and names the catalogued cause of a stop that fails (#965). Under goatlite, `doctor` and the browser step at phase 11 name the right phase and command, and a goatlite standup no longer points at an outside password manager or at `goatbuilder.yaml` (#965). A host group's own pin in `ops/pins/fleet-pins.yaml` now names the goatnet value it overrides (`over:`), so a group does not silently keep an old image after its goatnet moves; `goatbuilder pins` refuses a deviation with no `over:` (GB-358) or one whose `over:` no longer matches (GB-357), and prints the line to paste (#1089). On a peering declared `drivers: two`, phase 2 runs on the edge driver and the controller imports its result, and phase 14's acceptance can fire its probes on one machine and read the edge's trace from another; the edge's own leaf keys and the rest of the two-driver run are not built yet (#860, #961). *Changed exit codes:* an error that now carries GB-020, GB-025, GB-258, GB-277, GB-315, GB-320, GB-321 or GB-322 exits 1 (refused), where it exited 2 (usage), so the exit follows the contract's meanings; the newly coded errors with GB-005, GB-008, GB-024, GB-052, GB-254, GB-257, GB-259, GB-326, GB-359 or GB-365 still exit 2, and every other exit is unchanged (#870, #1093, #1139). This includes `goatbuilder grow` failing to write a grown config as YAML, and a failed wait for a standup phase, image pull or observability leg: both GB-322, both now exit 1. A YAML file goatbuilder reads from the checkout that does not parse (a pin table, the ladder, a record, a workflow), or an intent schema that is not JSON or does not compile, now stops with GB-329 and exits 1, where it was GB-254 with exit 2; a file that is missing or cannot be read stays GB-254 with exit 2 (#929). The new deploy refusals GB-382 and GB-383 exit 1, and a deploy dry run that would refuse now exits 1 where it exited 0 (#1225, #1226). No exit code the compatibility check keeps from 0.7.3 moves. If a script treats exit 2 as "the command line was wrong" and exit 1 as "refused", it now reads these errors correctly; a script that matched exit 2 or GB-254 for one of them should accept exit 1 and the new code as well, or better, read the `code` field of the `-o json` error document (`goatbuilder.error/v1`) instead of the exit number. From 1.0.0 the meanings of exit codes 0 to 4 are promised (ADR 1228), so a change like this one is made only before 1.0.0. *For a federation partner:* the partner conformance bundle (`ops/federation/bundle/`) has a new content digest, `6b26e2a6f17653cddea5ad200e57e6c51104c3a2f8ff7b198ff94726c493f05f` (it was `07b6039543f7c31e51e187808d88eb3bee436a052ef7c52ce47870609d9f38a6`). The only change is in the package specification: its tool row now names `goatbuilder federate` as the tool, built, with ADR 1225 accepted, where it named `goat federate`. No conformance vector changed. Take the new bundle with this release, so the digests both sides compare agree (#948). *Not yet in goatbuilder:* these rows of the 1.0 gate (`docs/design/goatbuilder-v1-gate.md`), among others listed there, are open: B3, a peering keeps carrying data after a key rotation; E3, `goatbuilder update` moves a 0.x install to 1.0 and back; I1 to I4, a joining site that runs the portal, the id console and the onboarding engine with every site writing; I6, a measured verdict for every write path to a replicated store; and J1 to J28, every machine kind as a build target (ADR 1257, Proposed), of which the parts listed above are built. *For someone contributing:* ADR 1257 (Proposed) and `docs/design/goatbuilder-build-targets.md` declare platform families and target types, and the 1.0 gate gains group J (#1091). `ops/ci/check-deploy-plays-reached.py` reports every deploy play no goatbuilder verb reaches, as a report for now (gate J28, #1211), and CI builds a VM for each target type from a cloud image to `doctor --target` (#1213, #1233). A changelog entry is committed alone, and the Unreleased section of `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md` is one pointer line; `python3 ops/release/changelog.py show` prints the entries as the next release will (#1033). The standup and teardown parity gates now print, for each differing line, its number and the column where the two lines first differ (#1181). The compatibility check is held to goatbuilder/v0.7.3 (#964). *To be removed:* nothing new. `goat federate <verb>`, deprecated in 0.5.0, is removed from `goat` no earlier than 2026-12-11 and only after one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.7.3.** *For someone deploying:* `goatbuilder federate directory` reads the peering directory (saltlick) and changes nothing: `ls` lists the directory's release and every party with the files it hosts, `show <party>` gives each hosted file's size and sha256, and `check <party> --for <counterparty>` checks each file a peering reads and names a missing one as `NOT HOSTED` (the party runs phase 5) or `ROUTE MISSING` (the directory's release does not serve the route), with GB-370, GB-371 and GB-372 (#1000). Every error `goatbuilder federate` raises carries its catalog code, so `goatbuilder explain <code>` answers each (#867). `goatbuilder explain release` and `explain fastlane` answer for each of their eight steps (#862). Phase 14's acceptance on a derived session learns the partner's challenge from a run stamp, so a rerun soon after a first run is no longer judged by the first run's challenge (#792). `join-node` names each declared service its run does not build (#953), and the end-state catalog declares the data router, admit-audit and SPIRE at a joining site (#968). *For someone contributing:* nothing new. *To be removed:* nothing new. `goat federate <verb>`, deprecated in 0.5.0, is removed from `goat` no earlier than 2026-12-11 and only after one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.7.2.** *For someone deploying:* `goatbuilder federate rotate <partner> ipsec-leaf` rotates an `ipsec-fips` peering's IPsec leaf. It runs phases 11 to 14 and passes the rotation to the edge role, `goat-peering-edge`, which checks the leaf an operator staged beside the live files, sets the live pair aside once, re-authenticates, and puts the old pair back if the IKE SA does not come up. `rotate <partner> ipsec-ca` also needs `--partner-holds-ipsec-ca <sha256>`, the partner's read-back of our new CA's fingerprint (GB-303). A stopped rotation resumes with the same id, and `--retire <id>` removes the set-aside key only once phase 14 has passed here (#763, #828). `federate rotate <partner> ca` is still refused with GB-282, and its message now says the CA rotation is decided (ADR 1242) but not built in this goatbuilder; rotate the leaves under the same CA with `rotate <partner> leaves` meanwhile (#894). A failed phase prints its fix once, on its `Fix:` line, and an INCOMPLETE phase 14 (X-ACCEPT-001) names `goatbuilder federate <peering> --from 14` to resume it (#911). `goatbuilder grow` hands a goatlite over to the full preset: it shows the difference leaf by leaf, the files it writes and hands over and the renderer command, asks (or needs `--yes`), then writes `ops/goatbuilder/goatbuilder.yaml`, takes the generated header off the files the goatlite's render wrote, and removes `goatlite.yaml`. It changes the checkout only, never a host, and refuses with nothing changed on GB-304, GB-305 or GB-306; it is step 3 of the growth design and has not run on hardware (#804). One behaviour change: the role now sets `make_before_break = yes` on every IPsec peering edge, so the first apply after this release restarts strongSwan once on each ipsec-fips edge and drops that peering's link briefly: apply both sides of a peering in one window (#763). *Known issue:* in 0.7.2, `goatbuilder federate rotate <partner> carrier` does not complete a carrier rotation, and the partner's acceptance then fails; on a peering with no carrier it reports success and changes nothing. Do not rotate a carrier key with 0.7.2. The fix is #839, not yet released. *For someone contributing:* the compatibility check is held to goatbuilder/v0.7.1 (#886). *To be removed:* nothing new. `goat federate <verb>`, deprecated in 0.5.0, is removed from `goat` no earlier than 2026-12-11 and only after one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.7.1.** *For someone deploying:* `join-node` builds a node in the Linux VM of an Android phone with `--class phone --via usb`, built on a fixture and not yet measured on a phone (#747); runs a joining site's own mesh DNS, so a site cut off from its founder still resolves the goatnet's service names (#678); refuses a node whose clock is off before changing it (#766); and, like `teardown`, keeps a timings file as `standup` does (#802). `standup` for a joiner site turns signal federation on with join-node's own steps (#824), and every timings row names its cause, with phase 11 timed and the slowest phases named (#805, #814). Every site's end state declares every service a cut-off site needs, and what a joining site does not run yet is named as a gap with the gate row that closes it (#671). `goatbuilder federate rotate <partner> leaves` replaces a running peering's leaves, and a leaf rotation that was interrupted finishes or rolls back (#689). `goatbuilder federate test <partner> --bilateral` completes the partner's half of acceptance on a session both sides derive from the agreement, opt-in (#720); phase 14's round trip resends fresh probes until one is acknowledged (#808), and in a bilateral session, our own staging row no longer fails by construction (#789). On a two-driver peering the edge driver runs phase 1's edge checks and phase 3's edge half and prints the way back (#717, #736). Backing out one of two peerings keeps the core leaf the other still uses (#716), and a back-out removes the peering's entry from the edge's host firewall (#788). After a signing-key rotation, phase 5 hands the peering directory over to the new key (#683). A host-allocation SKIP says which case it is and what clears it, and `federate plan --accept host-allocation` records a judged SKIP in the plan (#753, #779). The C3 comparison (`ops/goatbuilder/c3-agreement.py`) exits 2 and names a `verify` report that read no machine (#809). Acceptance on a derived session ignores a partner sample left by an earlier run (#786). `goatbuilder.yaml` takes three optional fields, `deploy.cloud`, `deploy.owner` and `deploy.cross_goatnet`; undeclared, nothing changes (#765). Three behaviour changes: an environment that declares `converger: pull-agent` is refused by `doctor` and by every verb that pushes to real hosts, with GB-307, until the pull converger is built (#803); `join-node` refuses a node whose clock is unsynchronized or more than 250 ms off, with GB-297 (#766); and a back-out with no other peering set up, and no record of what the core leaf's paths held before, stops with GB-293 where it stopped with GB-221 (#716). *For someone contributing:* a deprecated command, flag or value warns on stderr, and a report's `-o json` document lists it; the list is empty today (#798, #818); CI holds ADR 1228's deprecation period and kept exit codes once the last release is 1.0 (#800, #813, #826); a changelog entry title written in quotes renders without them (#764); the compatibility check is held to goatbuilder/v0.7.0 (#776); join-node's peer-groups query is measured against NetBird's own schema (#754); before tagging, a diff between the checked commit and the merge commit decides whether a stage runs again (#772). *To be removed:* nothing new. `goat federate <verb>`, deprecated in 0.5.0, is removed from `goat` no earlier than 2026-12-11 and only after one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.7.0.** *For someone deploying:* every refusal now names its error code, and an undeclared peering exits 1, refused, where it exited 2 (#560, #656). A failed phase of `federate`, `standup`, `join-node` or `deploy` names the error in its output with its fix and the command that runs the phase again (#646, #652, #669, #703). A run records every value it uses and where each came from, in `goatbuilder show` and `runs diff` (#649). Every verb's phases are in the phase catalog, and `goatbuilder explain <verb> <phase>` answers for each (#651, #703). `goatbuilder status` reads real hosts (#648), and `goatbuilder update verify-release` checks a downloaded release without installing it (#655). `join-node` names what a joining site does not run, adds a node at a third site, has no manual phase after reaching the node, and deploys a joining site's data router, its leaves, the health publishers it declares and, with signal federation off, its front door (#612, #613, #661, #699, #715, #718, #721). A back-out stops on a probe that cannot tell, takes back what admission placed, drops a role core partner's store whole, and says why when it stops after its plan (#554, #629, #668). `rollback --site` reaches a goatnet through its door, as `deploy` does (#644), and an edge deployed from a workspace gets the certificates it mounts, or phase 12 says why (GB-275, #658). Phase 10 places and restarts nothing when its admission is already in place (#692), and its deploy no longer refuses an approved plan for an edge with the host firewall baseline on (GB-188, #740); phase 13 keeps a partner's newer SPIFFE bundle (#698), and on a peering declared `drivers: two` the controller imports phase 1's edge result and runs its core half; the edge driver's own run is not built yet (#690). Site bootstrap installs the hub-directive applier at Spock sites that name a hub (#596). Container memory limits and Postgres memory are settable, and the roles that schedule with cron install it (#615). *For someone contributing:* a changelog entry is a file of its own and a new ADR's index row is rendered from the ADR (#623, #636); the compatibility check holds more of the last release, now goatbuilder/v0.6.1 (#676); contract clause C11 is written (#647); rotating the forwarder carrier keys and the WireGuard peering key is built as a library and in the roles, not yet on the command line (#667, #680); CI runs on `main` to the end. *To be removed:* nothing new. `goat federate <verb>`, deprecated in 0.5.0, is removed from `goat` no earlier than 2026-12-11 and only after one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.6.1.** A patch release. *For someone deploying:* a `goatbuilder federate` run killed in phase 11, after it wrote the WireGuard link's files and before it restarted the link, now resumes and brings the link up; in 0.6.0 this was a known issue (#597). The Ory deploy reads the Postgres password itself and never recreates `postgres-a` (#593), and the audit-subscriber's lifecycle steps run with a writable `HOME` (#595). A peering can declare `drivers: two`; such a run stops at the first phase that needs the edge and prints what the edge driver runs (GB-265), and the parts not yet built are refused before acting (GB-267). `federate <partner> --side edge` alone is now refused with GB-267, and `import` is a reserved peering name (#601). *For someone contributing:* the federation test environment's required job runs as stages (#602). *To be removed:* nothing new. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

**New in 0.6.0.** The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

*For someone deploying:* `goatbuilder update` verifies the release signature itself, with no `cosign` needed, and refuses a release whose signature does not verify (GB-261). Every run that drives hosts keeps a record, read with `goatbuilder runs`, `show` and `runs diff`. Every process goatbuilder starts is named, with its phase, command, host and log, before it prints anything, and a dry run prints the commands the real run executes. Each of federate's fourteen phases is described in one catalog. `goatbuilder explain federate <phase>` answers from it. A failed federate phase carries the matching error code and its fix. Several peerings each keep their own directory package by default (a behaviour change; a directory older than saltlick v0.5.0 keeps one package, so move it before adding a second peering). Admission keeps every other variable in the core's peerings file and refuses one it cannot read as literal entries (GB-237). A back-out reads the core the way admission wrote it, stops on anything it cannot read, and leaves the core's org fragment byte for byte as it was before admission. A run journal written by a later goatbuilder is read, not refused. The edge's checks read only the configuration path the core router names and refuse a key storage wider than the key-bundle grant; each stops when it cannot tell (a behaviour change). Values reach standup's and deploy's commands as one word each, and every error's "read more" path is a document that ships with goatcore. The isitup status page's probe list can be refreshed on its own, and a list behind its declaration is detected. Nothing half built ships switched on: what is not in 0.6.0 is listed in the changelog.

*For someone contributing:* every pull request checks configuration, commands, documents and error codes against the last release (gate rows A2 to A5). ADR 1228 sets the deprecation period, and the library that prints the warning is built. The 1.0 gate gains group H (a node on a phone) and group I (a joined site that runs cut off). ADR 1231 adds a stable line: the branch `stable` follows each whole-tree release `goatcore/vX.Y.Z`, and all work lands on `main`. Outside pull requests carry the label `community`. The federation test environment proves one directory package per partner against saltlick v0.5.0.

*To be removed:* `goat federate <verb>`, in the `goat` client, as announced in 0.5.0, no earlier than 30 days after 0.5.0 and not before a peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. Nothing in goatbuilder.

**New in 0.5.3:** the first published release since 0.5.1; 0.5.2 was tagged but its release did not run. It carries everything listed for 0.5.2 below, plus: the release workflows grant the permission their shared workflow needs; the goatlite administrator's address and `join-node`'s declared values reach their phases as one word each, and a bootstrap command missing its owner variable is refused; and `verify` reads a failed ledger read as unknown.

**New in 0.5.2:** the federation documents are corrected against the code, and GB-129 now says that a narrower `offer:` is refused only for a hand-written federation.toml. `status` reads the hosts themselves. Declared paths and profiles reach standup's phases as one word each. When the edge and the core are on separate hosts, the edge's ingress check now reads the core, and a check that cannot run stops phase 12 (a behaviour change). An interrupted phase 8 no longer leaves private keys in its staging directory. `validate` names GB-025 on every failing row, and `release` prints commits at a fixed 12 characters. CI no longer depends on the Ubuntu archive: when a runner cannot reach it, the jobs fail over to the project's own package cache.

**New in 0.5.0 and 0.5.1: federation is in goatbuilder.** (0.5.0 was tagged and not published; 0.5.1 is the same goatbuilder and the first published release that carries it.) You federate with a partner using goatbuilder alone. You make one decision (the partner, and the release sets it receives) and answer the run's prompts at phases 5, 6 and 10: the partner's key and CA fingerprint, the agreement digest, then the plan and what your core admits. The full list is in `crates/goatbuilder/CHANGELOG.md`.

- `goatbuilder federate <partner>`: the whole procedure in one run. At a terminal it asks for the partner's key and CA fingerprint and for the agreement digest. It makes the plan and asks you to approve it, shows what our core will admit and asks again, then carries on through acceptance. A run that stops resumes where it stopped.
- `goatbuilder federate plan <partner>`, `deploy <partner>`, `test <partner>`, `status [<partner>]` and `backout <partner>`: each stage on its own. `backout --dry-run` surveys what backing one peering out would remove.
- `goatbuilder federate allocate [<peering>]`: allocates one peering's values and renders its inventory, both deployment halves and its `federation.toml`. It runs beside peerings that are still written by hand.
- Admission on a core deployed by the goat-zenoh role: the role's own play, org fragment, router leaf and `zenoh_sovereign_peerings`. No restart command needs to be typed.
- Values come from the declarations the deployment already has:
  - `secrets.federation` for the signing key and CA;
  - `environments[].peering_directory` for the directory and its CA;
  - the site inventory for the peering's machines.

  `FED_*` variables stay as overrides.
- `goatbuilder federate init|lint|compose|diff|verify|apply` are the package verbs `goat federate` had, with the same flags and exit codes.
- **Deprecated: `goat federate`.** It still works in 0.5.0 and tells you the goatbuilder command to run instead. It will be removed from `goat` 30 days after this release, and not before one peering between two standing environments has been completed with `goatbuilder federate`. After that, `goat federate` only answers with an error that names `goatbuilder federate`. The script `ops/scripts/peering-standup.sh` stays as it is: documented, not supported.

**Assets.** `goatbuilder-linux-amd64`, `goatbuilder-linux-arm64` (both run on glibc 2.31 and later: Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11 and later), `goatbuilder-darwin-amd64` (Intel), `goatbuilder-darwin-arm64` (Apple Silicon), each with a `.sha256`; `goatbuilder-docs.tar.gz`, the goatbuilder book built from this tag, with its `.sha256`; `SHA256SUMS` over all five; `SHA256SUMS.cosign-bundle`, a keyless cosign signature over `SHA256SUMS` made by this repository's release workflow.

**Download, verify, install.** Replace `<tag>` with this release's tag and `<os>-<arch>` with `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, `darwin-amd64` or `darwin-arm64`.

```bash
base=https://github.com/USAREUR-AF/goatcore/releases/download/<tag>
curl -fL --remote-name-all "$base/goatbuilder-<os>-<arch>" "$base/SHA256SUMS" "$base/SHA256SUMS.cosign-bundle"
cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.cosign-bundle \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/USAREUR-AF/goatcore/\.github/workflows/_release-binary\.yml@refs/tags/goatbuilder/v' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS        # on macOS: shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
install -m 0755 goatbuilder-<os>-<arch> ~/.local/bin/goatbuilder
goatbuilder --version
```

The cosign step is optional and needs [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/system_config/installation/); the checksum step is not.

**macOS.** The binary is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. A copy downloaded with a browser carries the quarantine attribute and macOS refuses to open it; clear it once after the checksum passes: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/goatbuilder`. A copy fetched with `curl` has no quarantine attribute.

**Windows.** No Windows build; run goatbuilder from Linux, macOS or WSL.
